facts: The Next - Generation Secure Computing Base ( NGSCB ; codenamed Palladium and also known as Trusted Windows ) was a cancelled software architecture.
The Next - Generation Secure Computing Base ( NGSCB ; codenamed Palladium and also known as Trusted Windows ) was designed by Microsoft.

The Next - Generation Secure Computing Base ( NGSCB ; codenamed Palladium and also known as Trusted Windows ) aimed to provide users of the Windows operating system with better privacy, security, and system integrity.
The primary stated objective with NGSCB was to " protect software from software . ".
NGSCB relied on hardware designed by members of the Trusted Computing Group.
NGSCB used a new kernel called the " Nexus ".
Aspects of NGSCB have emerged in Microsoft 's BitLocker full disk encryption feature.
NGSCB would provide new applications with features such as hardware - based process isolation.
NGSCB would also facilitate the creation and distribution of digital rights management ( DRM ) policies pertaining the use of information.
The technology was the subject of much controversy during its development.
NGSCB was first demonstrated by Microsoft in 2003 at the Windows Hardware Engineering Conference.
The 2004 revision would enable applications written prior to its development to benefit from its functionality.
In 2005 , reports stated that Microsoft would scale back its plans so that the company could ship its Windows Vista operating system by its target date of 2006 .
Development of NGSCB spanned almost a decade before its cancellation.
